text:
jiayi: heads-up — seeing a spike in Pending pods for gpu-spot-1-x in us-central1-a. several nodes are stuck in PROVISIONING for ~12m and CA isn't creating replacements. errors in instance create: "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for region us-central1"

alex: thanks. checking autoscaler logs now. can you paste the exact pod failures?

jiayi: paste from kube-scheduler: 
```
Pod gpu-workload-58f7 Pending: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
Also from gcloud when CA tries to create instance: 
```
ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.insert) Some requests did not succeed:
 - Quota 'GPUS' exceeded. Limit: 100, used: 100.
```

infra-bot: [autoscaler] 2045678924 scale-up: group gpu-spot-1-x max=200 current=100 desired=101 failed -> quota 'GPUS' exceeded

maria: ah, region-level GPU quota hit. we've pushed a lot of long-running spot batches this week. two quick mitigations: (1) shift lower-priority batch pods to a smaller-gpu fallback pool (T4) if available, (2) temporarily bump dedicated-gpu pool for critical traffic. both costy but unblock.

cheng: I can wire a quick toleration/nodeAffinity swap for non-critical batch pods. suggestion: add a new nodeSelector label `gpu-type: t4-burst` and a toleration on the pod spec so CA can schedule into the t4 pool. snippet: 
```
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-fallback"
    operator: "Exists"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
  nodeSelector:
    gpu-type: "t4-burst"
```

alex: good. i'll also open a support ticket with cloud to request a quota bump but that's not instant. in the meantime i'll create an ephemeral nodepool `gpu-fallback-t4-ephemeral` with min=0,max=10 and label `gpu-type=t4-burst`. cost estimate ~ $1.8/hr per node.

jiayi: fine — prioritize creating the pool and migrating non-prod pods. for prod-critical latency jobs, we'll failover to dedicated-gpu-1 (already reserved). can someone own the migration runbook?

maria: i'll own runbook and post commands. quick checklist: 
- create nodepool: `gcloud container node-pools create gpu-fallback-t4-ephemeral --zone us-central1-a --machine-type n1-standard-8 --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 --enable-autoscaling --min-nodes=0 --max-nodes=10 --labels=gpu-type=t4-burst`
- taint existing fallback nodes: `kubectl taint nodes -l gpu-type=t4-burst gpu-fallback=true:NoSchedule` (so only tolerant pods land)
- patch batch deployment: `kubectl patch deploy batch -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu-fallback","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}],"nodeSelector":{"gpu-type":"t4-burst"}}}}}'`

cheng: I'll prepare the patch and run in canary (10% pods). also adding a PriorityClass for batch so we don't evict prod pods accidentally.

alex: after pool creation, CA should be able to scale the t4 pool under quota. follow-up: we should add a short-term quota monitor & alert so we don't hit region GPU limits again. opening a ticket: INFRA-6123.

jiayi: perfect. note for postmortem: consider adding a cross-region fallback policy (spread GPUs across us-central1-b) and a predictable bursting cap so we don't exhaust region quota with spots. also record cost delta for finance. :money_with_wings:
